the fumarate reductor of E. coli is composed of four polypeptides, two small hydrophobic polypeptides of 14,000 and 15,000 daltons, and two large hydrophilic polypeptides of about 69,000 and 27,000 daltons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fumarate reduction in E. coli is catalyzed by a membrane-bound enzyme that consists of four different polypeptides.
the fumarate reduction system of E. coli is a four-subunit complex composed of a catalytic-flavin-iron-containing subcomplex and two small membrane anchor polypeptide chains.
fumarate reduction in anaerobically grown E. coli is catalyzed by a membrane-bound enzyme that consists of four subunits, each of which has a distinct function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fumarate reductorase of Eschericha coli is a four subunit enzyme, not a two subunit one.
we have identified two new polypeptides that are required for fumarate reduction to occur in the membrane.
the fumarate reductorase is a four-subunit enzyme.
